questions.q: Tell me about a Salesforce or CRM setup you worked on. What did the business need and what did you configure?
questions.looks_for: Real configuration: objects, fields, page layouts, flows, reports, permissions. Explains the business need, their own part, and how users benefited.

questions.q: Describe a time users were unhappy with the CRM or not using it. What did you do to improve things?
questions.looks_for: Found the actual problem by talking to users, simplified screens or automated steps, gave training, and tracked adoption or feedback afterwards.

questions.q: A sales manager says her team can see records they should not see. How would you check and fix this?
questions.looks_for: Reviews organisation-wide defaults, role hierarchy, sharing rules, profiles and permission sets, tests with a sample user, fixes the most restrictive way, and confirms with the manager.

questions.q: When would you use automation like a flow, and when would you suggest custom code or no automation at all?
questions.looks_for: Uses clicks-based automation for most business rules, code only when logic is too complex or needs scale, and avoids automation that adds complexity without value. Mentions testing and maintenance.

questions.q: You need to import 50,000 customer records from spreadsheets into the CRM. How would you plan this?
questions.looks_for: Cleans and de-duplicates data, maps fields, tests with a small batch in a sandbox, plans for errors, takes a backup, then imports and validates counts and samples.

questions.q: A flow you deployed is sending wrong emails to customers right now. What do you do?
questions.looks_for: Deactivates the flow immediately, checks how many customers were affected, informs the manager, prepares a correction message if needed, fixes and tests in a sandbox before redeploying.

questions.q: Why do you want to work as a Salesforce / CRM admin, and what do you want to grow into? Please state clearly your notice period or joining date, and your expected salary in ₹ per month or per year?
questions.looks_for: Gives a genuine reason tied to the work, a sensible growth direction, a clear notice period or joining date, and a clear salary figure or range in ₹. Honest about buyout or negotiable notice if relevant.
